current_text.html: The people having answered these questions in the affirmative, by holding up their right hands, the candidate shall kneel, and the presiding minister shall, with prayer and the laying on of hands of the Presbytery, according to the apostolic example, solemnly set him apart to the holy office of the Gospel ministry. Prayer being ended, he shall rise from his knees; and the minister who presides shall first, followed by all members of the Presbytery, take him by the right hand, saying, in words to this effect: We give you the right hand of fellowship, to take part in this ministry with us. The presiding minister shall then say: I now pronounce and declare that __________________ has been regularly elected, ordained, and installed pastor of this congregation, agreeable to the Word of God, and according to the Constitution of the Presbyterian Church in America; and that as such he is entitled to all support, encouragement, honor, and obedience in the Lord: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. After which the minister presiding, or some other teaching or ruling elder appointed for the purpose, shall give a solemn charge to the pastor and to the congregation, to persevere in the discharge of their reciprocal duties, and then after prayer and the singing of a psalm, or hymn, the congregation shall be dismissed with the benediction. The Presbytery shall duly record its proceedings.3 3For assistant minister, add the word ‘assistant' before ‘pastor', and charge the Session rather than the congregation

relationships.title: Relationship of Assistant Pastor to the Church

occurrences.excerpt: An overture detailing how assistant pastors are called was found in conflict with BCO 3-2 and 12-2 through 12-4, as the relationship of an assistant pastor to a congregation is best left to the session.

relationships.title: Call of assistant pastor from another denomination without presbyterial examination

occurrences.excerpt: A session may not call an ordained assistant pastor from another denomination without presbytery approval and examination, as all teaching elders must be members of the serving presbytery.

relationships.title: Jennings v. North Florida Presbytery

occurrences.excerpt: …is entitled to all support, encouragement, honor, and obedience in the Lord" (BCO 21-7).

metadata.synopsis: North Florida Presbytery restored a minister deposed for adultery by a 19–17 vote. The SJC sustained the complaint, holding that Presbytery had not proceeded with the required caution and that a bare majority could not demonstrate BCO 34-8’s required strongly favorable general sentiment. It declined to require reordination, calling that question unsettled and treating BCO 37-5’s restoration pronouncement as sufficient pending clarification. The SJC annulled Presbytery’s actions concerning the minister and remanded for a proper probationary and review process.

relationships.title: Sherfey v. James River Presbytery

metadata.synopsis: Sherfey challenged James River Presbytery’s denial of his complaint and alleged errors in its commission’s proceedings. The SJC ruled the complaint judicially out of order with incurable defects: several grounds had not first been adjudicated by Presbytery as BCO 43-2 required, and the General Assembly filing missed BCO 43-3’s thirty-day deadline. Incorrect advice from Presbytery’s clerk did not excuse compliance. The adopted decision neither reached the merits nor ordered a remand; only a concurrence proposed returning the matter to Presbytery.

relationships.title: David Kniseley et al. v. Rocky Mountain Presbytery

metadata.synopsis: On complaint from TE David Kniseley and others, the SJC reviewed Rocky Mountain Presbytery's refusal to forbid a mission church from giving an unordained female staff member the title 'Minister of Church Life.' The SJC denied the complaint. It held the BCO uses 'minister' synonymously with pastor and teaching elder, but is silent on general use for non-ordained staff; a lower court may exercise discretion subject to BCO 40-2(3)'s WESP review. The decision addressed only the constitutional issue, not the title's wisdom or propriety; four commissioners dissented.
